Seed-san, by VirtualCast, Inc.

Fetched by the candidate's browser at runtime. CodeTrial does not redistribute
these bytes; the record below is the grant they arrive under.

Source:    https://github.com/vrm-c/vrm-specification
Path:      samples/Seed-san/vrm/Seed-san.vrm
License:   VRM Public License 1.0, https://vrm.dev/licenses/1.0/
Copyright: VirtualCast, Inc.
SHA-256:   624d0d554bc205bbdc33e22a68a2c3c20edebb3e573011ead8878a65e5329b23
Bytes:     10917800

CodeTrial renders this model as its interviewer, "Jim". The character is
VirtualCast's, not CodeTrial's, and is used under the grant below.

The grant travels inside the file. VRM Public License 1.0 takes its terms from
the VRMC_vrm.meta block of the model itself rather than from any web page, so
what follows is that block, read verbatim out of the bytes the SHA-256 above
pins:

  "name":              "Seed-san"
  "authors":           ["VirtualCast, Inc."]
  "copyrightInformation": "VirtualCast, Inc."
  "licenseUrl":        "https://vrm.dev/licenses/1.0/"
  "avatarPermission":  "everyone"
  "commercialUsage":   "corporation"
  "modification":      "allowModificationRedistribution"
  "allowRedistribution": true
  "creditNotation":    "required"

CREDIT IS REQUIRED. "creditNotation": "required" obliges any use of this model
to name its author. CodeTrial satisfies that by crediting VirtualCast, Inc. in
the lobby footer of web/index.html, in NOTICE, and here. It sat
beneath the avatar during the interview and was moved out because it crowded
the workspace. Moving it is fine; dropping it is not, and
tests/browser/avatar.test.js asserts a visible credit still exists in the UI.

Fetch the model by hand, as web/avatar/model.js does at runtime:

  curl -L -o Seed-san.vrm \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vrm-c/vrm-specification/837f156dbce43ad69183ce1bdab549961ae1c1ee/samples/Seed-san/vrm/Seed-san.vrm
  shasum -a 256 Seed-san.vrm

Re-read the embedded grant at any time:

  node -e 'const b=require("fs").readFileSync("Seed-san.vrm");
    const j=JSON.parse(b.slice(20,20+b.readUInt32LE(12)).toString("utf8"));
    console.log(JSON.stringify(j.extensions.VRMC_vrm.meta,null,2))'

Offline conversion retains the full humanoid skeleton and removes lower-body
render geometry. It exports two 1024x1024 color textures, calibrates non-metallic
skin and clothing materials, removes unused shape keys and revises aa to move
the jaw appearance, mouth corners, cheeks, lips and tongue together. The normal
and specular inputs are disconnected in the exported material setup. The v3
artifact retains ten morph targets, adding the source's left/right cheek-squint
and outer-brow targets to relaxed/happy. Mouth corners, cheeks and brows move
together, with reduced listening eyelid droop. The v2 jaw/blink shapes, base
surface, skinning, textures, materials and embedded permission metadata remain
unchanged. Conversion recipes and measured properties are preserved at the
pinned asset revision above; v3 is the artifact filename revision, while the
embedded metadata version remains 0.2.0-poc as exported.

The exporter writes the standard VRM Public License URL in licenseUrl and the
pinned Microsoft MIT notice in otherLicenseUrl. Both are disclosed above;
the full Microsoft grant is preserved below. Required credit is shown with the
existing model's credit in the lobby footer.
